title: Arrest & Police Rights in India
description: Essential constitutional and procedural safeguards every Indian citizen possesses if stopped, questioned, or detained by police officers.
whoItAppliesTo: All Indian citizens and residents facing police inquiry, detention, or formal arrest.
whatYouCanDo: Demand to see the police officer's identification badge and arrest memo; inform family or a lawyer immediately; exercise your right to remain silent beyond stating your name and address; demand to be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours.
importantPoints: Article 22(1) guarantees the right to know the grounds of arrest immediately.
Article 22(2) mandates production before the nearest Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time).
Section 47 of BNSS 2023 requires police to prepare a written Arrest Memo signed by at least one family member or respectable local witness.
Women cannot be arrested between sunset and sunrise except under extraordinary circumstances with prior written permission of a Judicial Magistrate.
misunderstandings: Myth: Police can beat or physically torture an accused to extract confessions. Fact: Custodial violence is strictly illegal under Indian Law; confessions made to police officers are inadmissible in court.

Myth: Police can keep an arrested person in custody indefinitely without court approval. Fact: Detention beyond 24 hours without a Magistrate's remand order is unconstitutional habeas corpus violation.
practicalSteps: Stay calm and do not physically resist the police officer.
Ask politely: 'Am I under arrest, or am I free to go?'
If under arrest, ask for the formal Arrest Memo and read it carefully before signing.
Immediately call your lawyer or a family member to notify them of your location and the station name.
Request a medical examination under Section 53 of BNSS upon arrest to document physical health.

faqs.q: Can police search my phone without a warrant?
faqs.a: Police cannot force you to unlock your personal digital devices without specific judicial authorization or a warrant in non-emergency situations.

title: Women's Legal Rights & Protections
description: Special legal safeguards enshrined under the Constitution of India, BNS, and specialized acts protecting women against domestic violence, workplace harassment, and illegal arrest.
whoItAppliesTo: All women in India regardless of age, marital status, religion, or employment status.
whatYouCanDo: File complaints under POSH Act at workplace Internal Committees; register Zero FIRs for assault; seek emergency protection orders under Domestic Violence Act 2005; claim free legal representation from DLSA.
importantPoints: Zero FIR Mandate: A woman victim of a sexual offence can register an FIR at ANY police station regardless of jurisdiction.
Sunset Protection: Under BNSS Section 43(4), women cannot be arrested after sunset and before sunrise except by a female officer with prior Magistrate sanction.
Right to Confidentiality: Section 72 of BNS prohibits publishing or revealing the identity of victims of sexual offences.
Workplace Protection: The POSH Act 2013 mandates an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) in every organization with 10+ employees.
misunderstandings: Myth: Domestic violence only applies to physical beatings. Fact: The Domestic Violence Act covers emotional, verbal, sexual, and economic abuse.
Myth: A woman must go to a police station to report harassment. Fact: Women can request a female police officer to come to their residence to record statements.
practicalSteps: For emergency help, dial 112 (National Emergency) or 1091 (Women Helpline).
For workplace harassment, submit a written complaint to your company's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) within 3 months.
Keep digital backups of emails, WhatsApp messages, or call logs as electronic evidence.

title: Consumer Rights & Redressal
description: Statutory rights guaranteed under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 to protect buyers against deceptive trade, defective goods, and deficient service providers.
whoItAppliesTo: Any individual who buys goods or hires services for personal use (excluding commercial resale).
whatYouCanDo: File consumer complaints online on e-Daakhil; claim full refunds, replacements, and financial compensation for mental harassment; report deceptive advertisements to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA).
importantPoints: Right to Safety, Information, Choice, Redressal, and Consumer Education.
Product Liability: Manufacturers and sellers are strictly liable for injuries or damages caused by defective products.
E-Commerce Coverage: Online marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, etc.) are strictly governed under E-Commerce Rules 2020.
misunderstandings: Myth: 'Goods once sold will not be taken back' stores tags are legally binding. Fact: Such disclaimers are unfair trade practices and invalid under Consumer Law.
practicalSteps: Always preserve tax invoices, receipts, and warranty cards.
Send a formal written Legal Notice to the company giving 15 days to resolve the grievance.
If unfulfilled, file a direct complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) app or e-Daakhil portal.

title: Cyber Rights & Digital Privacy
description: Rights shielding citizens against online financial scams, identity theft, cyberstalking, and unauthorized data breaches under the IT Act 2000.
whoItAppliesTo: All internet users, smartphone owners, and digital banking customers in India.
whatYouCanDo: Report financial cyber fraud within the 'Golden Hour' to helpline 1930 to freeze stolen funds; file complaints on cybercrime.gov.in; request removal of intimate images without consent.
importantPoints: Helpline 1930 connects directly to bank fraud monitoring nodes to freeze stolen amounts instantaneously.
DPDP Act 2023 grants citizens the right to data erasure and privacy consent withdraw.
misunderstandings: Myth: If you accidentally share an OTP, banks have zero liability. Fact: Reporting financial fraud immediately triggers cyber cell intervention and RBI limited liability guidelines.
practicalSteps: Call 1930 immediately within 1 hour of unauthorized bank transactions.
Take screenshots of transactional SMS, bank statements, and fraudster numbers.
